assumptions: The premium escalation rule (CaseEscalationService.levelFor) changes; the Escalation_Level__c picklist values are unchanged.
Account.Service_Level__c is the only seed: it is the field that defines who counts as a premium customer. Everything else the index reaches, it reaches from there.
Case.Escalation_Reason__c is excluded: it only feeds the comment body in recordEscalationReasons (CaseEscalationService.cls:71-82) and takes no part in choosing the level.

components.why: Defines who counts as a premium customer, so the rule change is checked against its values. It is the seed.
Holds the escalation rule (levelFor), which is the change itself. It reads Service_Level__c (CaseEscalationService.cls:48, :59).
Asserts the levels for premium and standard cases, so its expectations must follow the new rule. It sets Service_Level__c in setup (CaseEscalationService_Test.cls:29).
Should still pass unchanged: it goes through premiumCases, which filters only on Service_Level__c and never calls levelFor. It names Service_Level__c in setup (EscalationNotifier_Test.cls:29).
Agents must keep read access to the fields the rule uses. It grants Service_Level__c and the service class.
Team leads work escalated cases, so the rule change must respect their access. It grants Service_Level__c and the service class.
Account owners maintain Service_Level__c, so they decide who is premium under the new rule. It holds the field permission on the seed.
Dispatches case updates to the escalation service, so a signature change would break it. Shared with the assignment story DEMO-202; reached through CaseEscalationService.

Hidden invocable that creates the owner's follow-up task for premium cases; it relies on CaseEscalationService.premiumCases. A field search misses it because it reads no field; only the class-call chain reaches it.

Agents read the premium label, level and SLA state here; its state comes from getEscalationState, so a levelFor-only change needs no edit but the display is checked. A field search misses it; only the class-call chain reaches it.
Entry point for the whole chain; unaffected unless handler contexts change. A field search misses it; only the class-call chain reaches it.
Hidden flow that fires when a case reaches Level 2, so it follows any change to when Level 2 is set. It calls EscalationNotifier; a field search on Service_Level__c misses it.
Agents see the level and the escalation panel here. It hosts caseEscalationPanel; a field search on Service_Level__c misses it.
Runs the trigger path end to end and asserts Escalation_Level__c, so it must still pass after the rule changes. Reached through CaseTriggerHandler.

Holds the result of the rule (levelFor writes it); its picklist values stay as they are, so only its use is checked. Nothing reachable from Service_Level__c depends on the field as a node, so the index cannot reach it.
The open-hours threshold behind the Level 2 jump, passed into levelFor; the changed rule may read it differently.
Rejects an escalated case without a level; with unchanged picklist values it should still hold, but it is checked.
Offers the Escalation_Level__c values to premium support cases; unchanged values mean no edit is expected.
